Messages.Author: Wes

"LSJ" <vte...@white-wolf.com> wrote

>
> Not all abandoned games indicated on which turns they were abandoned.
> The following did, however:

<snip>

> So no, it doesn't look like length was a factor.

Well... Some moderators won't post the "final state" as the game
finishes. So for example you might have a game where everyone remaining
at that point decides to concede the game to one strong player and then
they all forget about it. It might therefore *look* like it was
abandoned, but it was only the actual recording of information near the
very end that was abandoned... this seems to happen a lot actually.

But that probably isn't true for most of those games. Frankly, I am
surprised to see so many abandoned games. And not very impressed! This
has not traditionally been a problem for me, and as most people know I
am probably one of the more prolific JOL players/moderators.

Still... I have to wonder what happened to the players in all of those
games...

Cheers,
WES

Hiya guys,
Further info for your survey:
Last WE, at Grand Vaulderie tournament:
Played 3 R+F.
2H time limit in the prelims, 2.5h in the finals.
I've only played 5 player tables.
4 tables I've played at:

round 1: 15 turns. I was ousted by Denis after 1 VP, right on the
verge of timelimit.2 players leftover in the game. Timeout after 2
hours
round 2: 15 turns. (5VP sweep). Finished in about 1.5h.
round 3: 13turns. Took 4 VP, missed one (my pred died to soon)Game
took about 1h15min.
Finals: 17 turns (or was it 18?)Took about 2h.15min. I believe
(Miller, can you confirm this?I know you kept track of it)

Average: 15+15+13+17=60turns/4rounds=15 turns per round.
Time average is kinda silly, since the finals went beyond the time
limit for the other rounds.

Personally, I believe the most important nuance in calculating this
"average"number of turns,is that there is an important difference
between:
"the number of turns *you* play", and "the number of turns the game
lasts".
In the simple calculation of averages, it's is simply not taken into
account that the game just doesn't last the same number of turns for
all players.
Ergo, I still think it's a realy bad idea to base a time limit for
turns on such calculations.
I'm not sure, but I think I saw Miller keep track of more stuff. With
any luck, he also kept the #of turns on other tables.

Greetz
Jo
